The proposed model represents a subject's face features as a linear combination of multiple quasi-phases, and learns a generator that outputs a set of basis images for each phase along with corresponding weighting networks. $$
\begin{cases}
\partial_{t}u(t,x)=D_{0}^{\alpha}(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u(t,x)+f(t), & (t,x)\in(0,T)\times\Omega, \\
f^{c}(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u(t,x)=0, & (t,x)\in(0,T)\times\partial\Omega, \\
u(0,x)=0, & x\in\Omega.
\end{cases}
$$
Here, $D_{0}^{\alpha}(-\Delta)^{\alpha}$ represents the combination of a spatial fractional Laplacian operator and a time fractional derivative of order $\alpha\in(0,1)$, while $\Omega$ denotes a bounded domain in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ where $n\geq 1$. The primary goal is to determine the time source term $f(t)$ based on either the source term in the equation or a time source term in the boundary condition. We will establish the well-posedness of this problem and develop a unique method to solve it. Additionally, we will discuss how the initial time and domain can be extended. A fractional-order Carleman estimate serves as a key tool in these analyses.
